heuristics.rule: Assess repair attempt success rate, not conflict frequency
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether a relationship is repairable...
heuristics.action: ...ask whether repair attempts after fights usually succeed or consistently fail in the same way, rather than counting how often fights occur
heuristics.because: Gottman's research shows it is the consistent failure of repair attempts — not the presence of conflict itself — that predicts an unhappy future

heuristics.rule: Treat contempt as a higher-order warning signal than other negative patterns
heuristics.condition: When one or more of the Four Horsemen are present...
heuristics.action: ...weight contempt disproportionately in the repairability diagnosis relative to criticism, defensiveness, or stonewalling
heuristics.because: Gottman's research identifies contempt as 'the greatest predictor of divorce' — more than any other single factor

heuristics.rule: Use the 5:1 positive-to-negative ratio as a quick relationship health gauge
heuristics.condition: When assessing the baseline emotional climate of a relationship...
heuristics.action: ...estimate whether positive interactions (gratitude, affection, small gestures) outnumber negative ones by at least five to one
heuristics.because: Gottman's longitudinal data links this ratio to relationship stability; falling below it correlates with deterioration

heuristics.rule: Require a minimum 20-minute timeout when physiological flooding occurs during conflict
heuristics.condition: When a partner becomes emotionally overwhelmed during an argument...
heuristics.action: ...institute a hard break of at least 20 minutes and avoid ruminating on grievances during it
heuristics.because: Research shows couples who took ~30-minute discussion breaks showed significantly lower heart rates and more positive subsequent interactions; ruminating during the break negates the benefit

heuristics.rule: Reframe complaints from character attacks to specific behavioral requests
heuristics.condition: When conflict communication defaults to criticism of who the partner is...
heuristics.action: ...shift to 'I' statements describing a specific behavior and an expressed need, not a verdict on character
heuristics.because: Criticism of character activates defensiveness and contempt; behavior-specific 'I' statements create space for repair rather than escalation

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Contempt is the single strongest predictor of divorce in Gottman's research — its presence shifts the repairability calculation more than any other variable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe whether interactions involve mockery, eye-rolling, sarcasm intended to demean, or expressions of superiority; distinguish this from frustration or criticism

decision_factors.why_it_matters: A relationship can survive the Four Horsemen if repair attempts reliably work; consistent repair failure — not conflict itself — is what predicts dissolution
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: after a fight, do attempts to de-escalate, apologize, or reconnect typically land and resolve the tension, or do they consistently fail or get rejected?

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The ratio of positive to negative interactions is one of Gottman's three core predictors of divorce; a depleted ratio means the emotional bank account cannot absorb conflict
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track over a representative week whether expressions of appreciation, affection, humor, and genuine interest outnumber criticisms, complaints, and dismissals by roughly 5:1

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Stonewalling, which shuts down repair, is often a physiological response to flooding — if a partner regularly floods and cannot self-soothe, sustained repair becomes structurally difficult
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether one or both partners regularly shut down, go silent, or disengage during conflict and whether they use structured breaks or simply withdraw permanently

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Defensiveness that never yields to any accountability blocks repair cycles; the antidote requires at least partial ownership, so willingness to take responsibility is a prerequisite for repair
decision_factors.how_to_assess: In recent conflicts, has either partner been able to say 'you're right about that part' even while holding their own perspective, or does every conflict end in mutual victimhood?

decision_factors.factor: Culture of appreciation vs. culture of grievance
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Regular small expressions of gratitude and affection are the antidote to contempt; their absence allows contempt to develop and deepen over time
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether partners spontaneously express gratitude, notice positive things about each other, and maintain affectionate small gestures in everyday life — not only during conflict resolution

hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Without active repair and positive interaction investment, the positive-to-negative ratio silently erodes; by the time open conflict surfaces, contempt may already be entrenched and the repair window much narrower
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Conflict-avoidant partners who interpret absence of fighting as relationship health

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Taking a timeout during flooded conflict
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: If the timeout is used for 'righteous indignation' rumination — mentally rehearsing grievances — it restores neither physiological calm nor relational goodwill, and the subsequent conversation may be worse than if no break had been taken
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Partners who intellectually know to take breaks but use the time to build their case rather than self-regulate

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Addressing the Four Horsemen without targeting contempt specifically
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Reducing criticism, defensiveness, and stonewalling while leaving contempt unaddressed leaves the highest-leverage predictor of dissolution in place; improvement on other dimensions may create false confidence about trajectory
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Couples in therapy or self-help efforts who measure progress by conflict reduction rather than by contempt elimination

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Statistically, a marriage can survive the Four Horsemen
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Survival is contingent on learning effective repair — the mere absence of divorce does not mean the relationship is healthy or stable; couples can remain together in chronic unhappiness if repair is partially but not fully restored
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Partners who use 'we're still together' as evidence that the relationship is on a good trajectory

failure_patterns.pattern: Diagnosing relationship health by conflict frequency rather than repair success
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Conflict is salient and countable; repair success is a process variable that requires deliberate observation and is easy to misattribute ('we made up eventually' vs. 'the repair attempt worked')
failure_patterns.consequence: Partners miss the actual predictive signal — consistent repair failure — and stay or leave based on the wrong metric
warning_signs: Saying 'we fight a lot but always get through it' without being able to describe how repair actually happens
Defining relationship quality primarily by how rarely or often arguments occur

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating contempt as equivalent in severity to the other Three Horsemen
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: All four are grouped together as 'bad communication patterns,' obscuring the research finding that contempt is uniquely and most strongly predictive of dissolution
failure_patterns.consequence: Effort gets distributed evenly across all four patterns; the highest-leverage problem receives insufficient attention and the relationship continues to deteriorate
warning_signs: Therapy or self-improvement work focuses on 'not being defensive' or 'not stonewalling' while mockery, eye-rolling, and superiority framing continue
Progress reports that list improvements in three of the four Horsemen without addressing contempt

failure_patterns.pattern: Ruminating on grievances during a conflict timeout
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The physiological need for a break is recognized, but the cognitive habit of case-building is not interrupted; the break is experienced as preparation for continued argument rather than genuine self-regulation
failure_patterns.consequence: Heart rate and emotional flooding do not resolve; the resumed conversation reescalates faster, and stonewalling may become permanent withdrawal
warning_signs: Returning from a timeout with new arguments or evidence rather than reduced emotional intensity
Timeouts consistently lasting much longer than 30 minutes because neither partner feels ready to re-engage

failure_patterns.pattern: Using 'you' statements disguised as 'I' statements during conflict
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The surface form of 'I feel that you...' is adopted without internalizing the underlying shift from character attribution to self-disclosure of need; the criticism is merely rephrased
failure_patterns.consequence: The partner registers the criticism and responds defensively; the Gentle Start-Up antidote fails not because the approach is wrong but because it was not actually implemented
warning_signs: Statements that begin with 'I feel' but immediately name partner behavior or intent: 'I feel like you never listen'
Partner's defensive reaction to what the speaker believes was a non-critical statement

diagnostic_questions.question: When you try to repair after a fight — apologize, de-escalate, reconnect — does it usually work, or does it usually fail the same way?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the relationship has a functioning repair mechanism; this is the core predictor variable Gottman identifies as distinguishing repairable relationships from those heading toward dissolution
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What does a successful repair look like — who initiates, what do they do, how long does it take?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: How does it fail — does one partner reject the attempt, does it escalate, or does the repair seem to work but the same issue resurfaces unchanged?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is there mockery, eye-rolling, sarcasm meant to demean, or a sense that one partner views the other with contempt?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the highest single predictor of divorce is present; this distinguishes a conflict-heavy but repairable relationship from one where the emotional foundation has been fundamentally eroded
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: How long has contempt been present, and does the other partner recognize and name it as contempt or reframe it as humor or frustration?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Which of the remaining three Horsemen are present, and is there evidence of active repair culture to offset them?

diagnostic_questions.question: In a typical week, do positive interactions — appreciation, affection, humor, genuine curiosity about each other — outnumber negative ones by roughly five to one?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The current state of the emotional bank account; a depleted ratio means the relationship lacks the buffer to absorb conflict and repair is harder to initiate and receive
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Are the positive interactions spontaneous and mutual, or concentrated in one partner or in scripted/obligatory moments?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: When did the ratio shift, and was there an identifiable event or a gradual drift?

diagnostic_questions.question: When one partner raises a complaint, does it typically come out as a description of a specific behavior and a stated need, or as a verdict on the other person's character?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether criticism has escalated into character-level attack, which is harder to respond to non-defensively and more likely to invite contempt over time
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Does the partner receiving the complaint typically respond with acknowledgment or with counter-complaint?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Does the person raising complaints recognize this pattern, or do they believe they are communicating specific needs?

diagnostic_questions.question: When one partner shuts down or goes silent during conflict, does the other interpret this as rejection, or do both partners have a shared understanding of what is happening and what to do?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether stonewalling is understood as a physiological flooding response (which has a structural antidote) or is experienced as abandonment (which triggers escalation and makes repair harder)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Do they have an agreed timeout protocol, and does it get used consistently?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: How does the non-stonewalling partner respond — pursue, escalate, or also withdraw?

industry_realities.common_belief: Conflict itself is the problem — healthy relationships have little or no fighting
industry_realities.actual_reality: Gottman's longitudinal research shows all relationships have conflict; the differentiating variable is not whether conflict occurs but whether repair attempts consistently succeed afterward
industry_realities.implication: Evaluating a relationship by how much it fights is the wrong diagnostic; couples should instead assess the quality and success rate of their repair cycles

industry_realities.common_belief: If a couple is still together and not miserable, the relationship is on a stable trajectory
industry_realities.actual_reality: A marriage can statistically survive the Four Horsemen — meaning it does not end in divorce — while remaining chronically unhappy; survival and health are distinct outcomes
industry_realities.implication: Remaining together is not sufficient evidence of repairability; the presence of contempt and failed repair attempts must be assessed independently of whether the couple has separated

industry_realities.common_belief: Contempt is one of several equally serious communication problems to address
industry_realities.actual_reality: Gottman's research identifies contempt as the single greatest predictor of divorce — qualitatively different in predictive power from the other three Horsemen
industry_realities.implication: In any repair effort, eliminating contempt deserves disproportionate attention; progress on the other three Horsemen without addressing contempt leaves the most dangerous factor in place

industry_realities.common_belief: Taking a break from a heated argument automatically helps the situation
industry_realities.actual_reality: A break only helps if it is used for genuine physiological self-soothing; ruminating on grievances during the break — 'righteous indignation' — fails to lower heart rate and can make the subsequent conversation worse
industry_realities.implication: Couples need to actively structure what happens during timeouts, not just agree to take them; the quality of the break determines whether it functions as a repair mechanism

industry_realities.common_belief: Divorce prediction from communication patterns requires extensive professional observation
industry_realities.actual_reality: Gottman's methods predicted divorce with over 90% accuracy using observable variables — interaction ratio, presence of the Four Horsemen, and physiological measures — making this a practically usable diagnostic framework, not just a research tool
industry_realities.implication: Individuals can apply a structured version of this framework to their own relationship rather than relying solely on subjective feelings of happiness or unhappiness

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Primary diagnostic question used to assess relationship health
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Asks 'are you happy?' or 'do you fight a lot?' as the central evaluative question
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Asks 'when you attempt to repair after a conflict, does it consistently work or consistently fail?' as the central diagnostic
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Happiness is a lagging and subjective indicator; repair attempt success rate is the leading and behaviorally specific predictor Gottman's research identifies — using the wrong metric produces systematically wrong assessments

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Treats criticism, contempt, defensiveness, and stonewalling as roughly equivalent problems requiring balanced attention
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Treats contempt as categorically more serious and prioritizes its elimination before addressing the other three
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Evenly distributed effort leaves the highest-leverage variable under-addressed; expert triage concentrates effort where the research shows it matters most

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Interpreting the absence of divorce or separation
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Uses continued cohabitation or lack of formal separation as evidence that the relationship is functioning or repairable
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Treats survival and health as independent variables; assesses whether repair mechanisms are functioning regardless of whether the couple has formally separated
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Conflating survival with health leads to false reassurance; a relationship can be statistically 'surviving' while on a clear deterioration trajectory

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Recommends 'take a break when things get heated' as a standalone intervention
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Specifies that the break must be at least 20 minutes, must be used for genuine self-soothing rather than grievance rehearsal, and reconnection should follow a structured protocol
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: A poorly executed timeout can worsen outcomes; the mechanism only works if its specific conditions — duration, cognitive content during the break, re-engagement — are met

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Teaches the surface form — 'say I feel instead of you always' — and treats adoption of the form as successful implementation
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Distinguishes between genuine self-disclosure of need and criticism disguised in 'I feel' syntax; checks whether the partner's response indicates the message landed as non-critical
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: The antidote to criticism works only if it achieves the underlying shift from character attribution to behavioral specificity and need expression; form compliance without substance compliance leaves the Horseman in place
